TAGLINE: Mechanistic pruning experiments for separating compression that preserves general perplexity from compression that preserves reasoning circuits.
OVERVIEW: A structured pruning + activation healing pipeline (TIM-MGDT) that identifies which transformer layers and MLP widths are elastic, critical, or reasoning-specific. The current focus is Mistral-7B compression that survives GSM8K rather than merely preserving C4 perplexity.

Phase 16 showed the central failure mode: 20% hardware-aligned width pruning kept C4 perplexity in a plausible range but collapsed 5-shot GSM8K from 38.7% to about 5%. That is a useful negative result because it separates general language retention from reasoning-circuit retention.

Phase 19 validation. Uniform structural width pruning collapses GSM8K even at 1%, but dense-shaped magnitude masks preserve reasoning at much higher sparsity. The strongest current positive control is 20% mask sparsity with 37.2% full GSM8K versus 38.7% dense.
RESEARCH_Q: Why does dense-shaped magnitude masking preserve Mistral-7B GSM8K reasoning at 20-30% sparsity while structural MLP-width pruning collapses at 1-5% despite similar C4 perplexity?
RUNS: Phase 15 — True Layer Dropping & Boundary Healing
DECISIONS: We shifted focus to Mistral-7B and Llama-3-class architectures, where compression failures are meaningful for modern reasoning deployments.
Phase 18B and Phase 19 now form a controlled contrast: C4-matched structural and masked models can have very different GSM8K retention.
To ensure theoretical FLOP reductions translate to physical speedups, we round pruned MLP dimensions to nearest 64 (Tensor Core alignment) via specific ceil/floor strategies.
